title: [Chapitre] V. Algèbre des figures : notes manuscrites (14/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting (pp. 18-20). L is a set. A 'figure ensembliste' F in L is a family of subsets of L (strata, or their closures) with some stability property, presumably under intersections. For A in F, the interior A° is A minus the union of the elements of F strictly contained in A. In the motivating case (p. 18), L is the poset of cells of a closed stratification (X_x), x in L, of a triangulable space X, for instance a regular cell complex. For a down-closed ('fermée', admissible) part A of L one sets X_A = ⋃_{x∈A} X_x. The map A ↦ X_A is a bijection between the closed parts of L and the closed subsets of X that are unions of strata X_x°.

Page 19, first part. It is therefore enough to consider figures Φ all of whose elements are closed in L, i.e. Φ ⊂ F_fermés(L). An element of ΛF obtained this way (ΛF is apparently the set or lattice of such figures) can be read as a geometric datum on X. It is a maximal admissible family of closed subsets of X that is stable under ∩ and adapted to the stratification (X_x°): each member is a union of closed strata. In a terminology Grothendieck calls 'discutable', such a datum is a 'subdivision' of X, or more exactly of its support in X. This is the combinatorial shadow of a cell decomposition: a lattice of closed unions of cells, as with the face poset of a CW/polyhedral complex in its Alexandrov topology.

Page 19, second part. Given two set-theoretic figures F, G in L, he will define when F is a refinement of G and when F is a subdivision of G. Proposition (equivalent conditions):
- (a) For every A ∈ F, the set G^A = {B ∈ G : A ⊂ B} has a smallest element φ(A). This gives a map φ : F → G, automatically increasing. In addition (continued p. 20), for A ∈ F and B ∈ G, A ∩ B is a union of elements of F, a closure condition relative to |F|.
- (b) For every A ∈ F there is B ∈ G with A° ⊂ B°. Such a B is unique, written φ(A), and φ is increasing.

Page 20 proves (a)⇒(b). It takes x ∈ A°, uses the union condition to find A' with x ∈ A' ⊂ B' ∩ A, deduces A' = A, and concludes by minimality. It then starts (b)⇒(a) via A = ⋃_{A'⊂A} A'°.

In modern terms, φ is the 'carrier' map of a subdivision: each cell of the finer complex lies in the relative interior of a unique smallest cell of the coarser one, and the carrier map is order-preserving. The two conditions say that 'smallest containing closed cell' coincides with 'cell whose open interior contains the open cell'. This serves Grothendieck's 1986 project of an 'algebra of figures': a purely combinatorial/lattice-theoretic framework for stratified ('tame') spaces and their subdivisions.
errors: The (a)⇒(b) proof on p. 20 silently uses the extra 'de plus' condition: B'∩A is a union of elements of F. Without that hypothesis the equivalence fails, so it is essential, and it is only partly written on p. 19.
Uniqueness of B in (b) is called 'évident'. It relies on the open strata B° of G being pairwise disjoint, which needs G to be closed under ∩ (or a similar condition) and is not stated on this page.
The interpretive paragraph is admitted by Grothendieck to use 'discutable' terminology and is somewhat loose about 'subdivision' versus 'induced on the support'.

ideas.what: Closed (down-set) parts of the cell poset correspond bijectively to closed unions of strata of X. Figures can be restricted to families of closed parts, interpreted as subdivisions of X.
ideas.modern_name: Face poset / Alexandrov topology of a regular cell complex; subcomplexes as order ideals
ideas.usually_credited_to: Alexandrov (1937), McCord (1966), Björner (1984) for regular CW complexes

ideas.what: Refinement/subdivision between two set-theoretic figures, with equivalence of 'smallest containing element' and 'open interior contained in open interior', yielding a monotone map φ: F→G.
ideas.modern_name: Carrier map of a subdivision of a polyhedral/regular CW complex (poset subdivision)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Classical PL topology; formalized combinatorially by Stanley (1992, local h-vectors), Björner and others

missed.claim: Part of Grothendieck's 1986 'Algèbre des figures' programme: an axiomatic set/lattice-theoretic theory of figures, stratifications, refinement and subdivision, meant as a foundation for tame topology. The specific results here are classical in substance.
missed.quote: Soient F et G deux figures ensemblistes dans L. On va définir quand F est un raffinement, et quand c'est une subdivision de G.
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Of mainly historical interest. It documents Grothendieck's combinatorial approach to stratified spaces, linked to the 'topologie modérée' of Esquisse d'un programme. Mathematically it overlaps with known theory of face posets and subdivisions.

deep.surprise_reason: Routine combinatorics of cell posets and subdivisions (carrier maps). Interesting only as part of an unpublished foundational programme; no new result.
transcription_corrections: 'Donc on a pourra dire aux Φ ∈ F' should read roughly 'Donc on pourra se borner aux Φ ∈ F telles que les A ∈ Φ soient fermés dans L'.
'stables par G relativement d'équations [?] [-collection-]' is more likely 'stables par ∩, relativement à la stratification (X_x°)'. The crossed-out 'collection' is replaced by 'stratification'.
'i.e. disjointes [?] de réunion des [?] disjointes fermées de X' reads roughly 'i.e. d'objets ... réunions de strates fermées de X'.
'reconnaître une donnée de X comme une "subdivision"' is likely 'une manière de voir X comme une "subdivision"'.
'(ou plutôt, divisé sans leurs supports dans X)' is likely '(ou plutôt, induit sur leurs supports dans X)'.
The margin note at bottom left is roughly 'cela redonne [?] ΛF(C(G))' rather than 'cf. aussi'.
In (a), the hand-written forms 'G_A' / 'G^A' are corrected to G^A with superscript.
